html:
Georgia came under the Russian Empire in 1801, when Tsar Paul I annexed the eastern kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti, and by 1878 Russia held all the Georgian lands.

The east had sought Russian protection in the Treaty of Georgievsk of 1783, but Russia did not defend it when the Persian shah sacked Tbilisi in 1795. Russia then abolished the Bagrationi monarchy and the independence of the Georgian church. Western Georgia was taken in steps. Russian rule brought peace from Persian and Ottoman raids, a railway and, later, Baku oil passing through to the Black Sea. It also brought Russification, which provoked the national revival of Ilia Chavchavadze. Georgia left the empire in 1918 as the Democratic Republic of Georgia.
sum: Georgia came under the Russian Empire in 1801, when Tsar Paul I annexed the eastern kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti, and by 1878 Russia held all the Georgian lands.
